questions.question: During a night-time crying episode, at what point would a parent most naturally hold the phone near the cot and let it listen?

options.label: Straight away, before trying anything
options.belief_phrase: right at the start, before anything is tried

options.label: After the first thing they try has not worked
options.belief_phrase: once the first attempt has failed

options.label: After several attempts, when they are out of ideas
Only once the baby has been crying for a long time
It would not fit into the episode at all

questions.respondent_note: Respondents will be asked about their own last episode, never this.

questions.question: Compared with how a parent copes today, what would have to be clearly more for them to prefer a suggestion from the app?

options.label: Fewer things tried before the baby settles
options.belief_phrase: that fewer things tried before the baby settles

options.label: A shorter time until the baby settles
Less worry and second-guessing while it is happening
Less need to wake or call on someone else
options.belief_phrase: less need for a second pair of hands

options.label: Less strain afterwards, such as getting back to sleep

questions.respondent_note: Respondents will be asked about their own last episode, never this.

questions.question: At 3 a.m., how much extra effort would a parent put into getting the app listening before giving up on it?

options.label: None; it must work with the phone already in hand
A few taps, such as opening the app and pressing listen
A short one-time setup, then one tap each night
options.belief_phrase: a one-time setup, then a tap

options.label: A longer setup, such as entering the baby's details, if done in the daytime
options.belief_phrase: a proper setup done in the daytime

questions.respondent_note: Respondents will be asked about their own last episode, never this.
